t: Tāufaʻāhau, baptised as George, ended half a century of civil war and united Tonga as King George Tupou I in 1845–1852.
His 1862 code freed commoners from forced service to chiefs, and his 1875 constitution, still in force, forbade the sale of land.
A British protected state from 1900 to 1970 but never a colony, Tonga remains a monarchy under King Tupou VI.
dyk: Tonga regained full independence on 4 June 1970, the 108th anniversary of George Tupou I’s 1862 code freeing commoners from forced service to their chiefs.
ev: Tāufaʻāhau defeats Laufilitonga at the Battle of Velata on Lifuka
Tāufaʻāhau becomes Tuʻi Kanokupolu and King George Tupou I
The fall of Pea and Houma ends the civil wars on Tongatapu
George Tupou I’s code frees commoners from forced service to chiefs
The constitution makes Tonga a constitutional monarchy
A Treaty of Friendship makes Tonga a British protected state
Tonga regains full independence and joins the Commonwealth
Reforms give the people a majority of elected seats in parliament
